function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Reconstruct the Internet Research Agency's 2016 United States social-media influence operation using only evidence returned by benchmark tools. Retrieve and preserve the exact source IDs those tools return, and do not invent or supplement citations. Focus on: Department of Justice indictment facts and explicitly labeled allegations; United States Senate findings and explicitly labeled official assessments; social-media platform disclosures and data; identified organizations, individuals, personas, pages, groups, handles, domains, and accounts; organizational structure and funding information; operational methods; a supported timeline; target audiences; political messaging; and campaign objectives. For every proposed identity or relationship among people, entities, accounts, events, funding flows, platforms, personas, and objectives, state whether it is documented fact, allegation, official assessment, inference, or uncertain, and link it only when the returned evidence supports it. Explicitly identify corroboration across Department of Justice, Senate, and platform evidence, gaps, and contradictions, including differences in scope, dates, attribution, account counts, or characterization. Keep unspecified dates, actors, platforms, personas, funding details, objectives, and relationship types open rather than filling them in. Return a structured evidence dossier suitable for a final Markdown report, with concise quotations or faithful paraphrases, exact source IDs, and a note for each important conclusion explaining its evidentiary status. Do not cite anything whose source ID was not returned by the benchmark tools."}
function.name: ConductResearch
